note: §6.26 `full` is a continuous-trim upper bound; this suite closes the loop with finite trim codes, an injected readout noise and an actuator gain error, then recomputes P on the same 3 anchors x 32 points x 48 draws

checks.name: E1 the step is 2R/2^(Nc+Nf) and the code count is 2^(Nc+Nf)
E2 every command lands within step/2 and the code set is the uniform step grid
checks.detail: max |res| 3.416e-04 = 0.50 step; max grid deviation 1.1e-13 step

checks.name: E3 overlap: the analytic worst residual at the nominal fine gain IS step/2; a -25 %% fine-gain error opens a 0.25-LSB gap, grows the worst residual 16x, and a 25 %% overlap is exactly what absorbs it
checks.detail: nominal max 0.0342 % = step/2 exactly (analytic); -25 % gives 0.5469 % = 16.0x the nominal (predicted gap 0.25 LSB = 1.09 %)

checks.name: E4 a quantization-limited loop: max <= step/2 and RMS = step/sqrt(12)
E5 read noise adds in quadrature and is NOT dithered away: RMS = sqrt(step^2/12 + sigma^2) over four decades, and it keeps growing once sigma > step
checks.detail: worst deviation 1.3 % for sigma 0.003..30 step; at sigma=30 step the RMS is 30.4 step, i.e. the measurement (step/2 = 0.5 is not a bound)

checks.name: E6 the actuator-gain ladder: one pass leaves e*delta and each retry multiplies by e (with quantization removed the law is exact)
E6b a retry saturates: k=3 changes nothing measurable and k=2 already sits at/below the code floor, so k_max=2 is the right loop budget
checks.detail: k=1 6.302e-03 -> k=2 3.516e-05 (code floor step/2 = 3.418e-04) -> k=3 3.516e-05 -> k=4 3.516e-05: two passes reach the floor, further passes are bit-exact no-ops

checks.name: E7 the held-out VERIFY is a probabilistic gate: MC matches Phi((tol-r)/sigma) - Phi((-tol-r)/sigma) at every r; a chip at r = 1.0 tol is accepted only ~50 %% of the time
checks.detail: worst |MC - analytic| = 0.64 s.e. (MC n=4000); r=1.0 tol accepts 0.492

checks.name: S1 one joint knob cannot trim 3v3 to 1 %: the measured self/gain separation exceeds the 1 % workload at 9 of the 16 3v3 points (worst 6.12 % at 3v3:jt_3v3_ff_p125)
checks.detail: worst 6.12 % at 3v3:jt_3v3_ff_p125 vs the 1 % workload; 6v0 worst 16.02 % at 6v0:jt_6v0_ff_p125 -- the knob count, not the DAC bit count, is binding

checks.name: S2 the required trim range is the measured worst deviation, not a round number: +-34.4 % (a +-25 % DAC clamps real chips)
checks.detail: 3v3 29.6 %; 6v0 34.4 %; with +-25 % those chips are REJECTED by VERIFY, not silently trimmed

checks.name: E8b the 12-bit option meets the plan's <2.5x spec: realized residual 122 ppm = 1.22x the 100 ppm floor
checks.detail: 10-bit gives 296 ppm (3.0x); 12-bit gives 122 ppm (1.22x) -- the readout floor, not the DAC, now dominates

checks.name: E8 the readout is not the bottleneck: sigma_read <= the DAC step/2
checks.detail: sigma 221 ppm vs step/2 342 ppm -- quantization-limited, so extra ADC bits buy nothing until the DAC gains a bit; the realized RMS residual is 296 ppm (3.0x the ideal 100 ppm)

checks.name: E10 the QoI gain is linear in the residual over two decades, and it is NOT 1: the edge/mirror axis is amplified
checks.detail: diffusion-1d gmax 1.0; poisson-2d gmax 0.0; burgers-1d gmax 13.4 -- a 1 %% coefficient residual on the edge axis is a >5 %% QoI residual on at least one anchor, so a coefficient-space verify is too loose

checks.name: E9 a global trim cannot touch per-DEVICE mismatch: with one mismatch draw per node the untrimmable floor is >=3x the global-trim residual at every anchor
checks.detail: diffusion-1d 11.2x; poisson-2d 83766946933637.6x; burgers-1d 10.3x -- §6.26's `full` assumes a global trim; that granularity, not the DAC, is the next budget item

checks.name: T1 a coefficient-space verify at 1 % does NOT reproduce the ideal full column: trim2 loses the 1 % column at 34 of 96 cells (worst P1 0.00) -- the QoI gain is the missing factor
checks.detail: min P1: ideal 1.000 vs trim2 0.000; the losses sit on the anchor whose edge axis is amplified 12.5x

checks.name: T1q a QoI-weighted verify (each axis <= tol/(2*gmax)) plus a 12-bit DAC/readout lifts the 1 % column from 0.00 to >=0.75 at every cell
checks.detail: min P1: trim2 0.00 (coefficient verify) -> trim_q12 0.792 (QoI verify, 12 bit); the residue is the false-reject rate of the tight gate, not a residual error

checks.name: T2 dropping the retry costs the 1 % column at 38 cells (the 3 % actuator error, not the DAC, is the cost)
checks.detail: diffusion-1d 6v0:jt_6v0_ff_p125 P1 0.98 (1.0 passes avg); poisson-2d 3v3:jt_3v3_ff_m40 P1 0.98 (1.0 passes avg); poisson-2d 6v0:jt_6v0_ff_m40 P1 0.85 (1.1 passes avg) -- worst cell at 2 %/5 % over all 96: 0.00/0.00

checks.name: T3 one joint knob costs the 1 % column at 64 cells (the measured self/gain separation, not the DAC, is binding)
checks.detail: diffusion-1d 3v3:3v3_ff P1 0.04 P2 0.04; diffusion-1d 3v3:3v3_ss P1 0.17 P2 0.17; diffusion-1d 3v3:3v3_tt P1 0.94 P2 0.94; diffusion-1d 3v3:jt_3v3_ff_m40 P1 0.79 P2 0.79

checks.name: T4 fail-closed accounting: no cell scores more passes than it has verified chips
checks.detail: rejections of 4608 draws per mode: trim2 2, trim1shot 15, trim1knob 2202, trim_q 1178; clamp events 11/11/11/11; 0 cells exceed their verified fraction

checks.name: T5 the QoI gate's yield loss is analytic: the trim residual is noise accumulated over k passes and VERIFY adds one more draw, so P(reject) = 2(1-Phi(tol/(sigma sqrt(k+1))))
checks.detail: tol 373 ppm, sigma12 112 ppm, mean k 1.6 -> predicted 4.0 %, measured 5.0 % (ratio 1.26); the 10-bit sigma 221 ppm would put this gate at 1.7 sigma and reject most good chips
